findings: The primary specimen is identifiable as a typical blue-bar Rock Pigeon: stocky body, small head, short pink-red legs, blue-gray plumage, two black wing bars, green-to-purple neck iridescence, pale cere, orange eye, and dark-tipped tail all agree with the references and direct sources.

The primary specimen contains one head, one bill, one tail, two convincingly attached legs with intact anisodactyl feet, and one visible near-side wing; the far-side wing is naturally occluded by the side-profile pose.

The bill is correctly short and essentially straight, with a pale fleshy cere. Both depicted heads have coherent upper and lower mandibles traced from a shared base to a natural, nearly co-terminal tip; neither bill is truncated, reversed, or inconsistent with the reference profiles.

The eye, head-to-body proportions, breast, neck, folded wing, tail, legs, and feet are anatomically coherent. The folded tail is compatible with the species' broad, rounded tail structure and retains a dark terminal region.

The detached wing and head are clearly intentional supplementary studies rather than extra birds or parts attached to the primary specimen. Each study is anatomically coherent and consistent with the primary rendering.
All visible identification text is spelled correctly and matches the proposed profile: “Rock Pigeon,” “Columba livia,” “Columbidae,” and all six field-mark statements are intact and meaningful.
The three measurement lines exactly match the independently verified All About Birds values: length 11.8–14.2 in (30–36 cm), wingspan 19.7–26.4 in (50–67 cm), and weight 9.3–13.4 oz (265–380 g).

The habitat paragraph agrees with direct sources describing rocky cliffs and ledges, farmland and fields, towns or cities, built structures, and nesting in sheltered ledges, nooks, crevices, or recesses.

The behavior paragraph is supported across the direct sources: flocking, daylight ground foraging, walking or running with head movement, eating seeds and fruit, strong steady direct flight, bowing/cooing/inflated-throat strutting, and care of young by both parents.

The vertical measurement diagram is internally consistent: 11.8 in (30 cm) is the lower endpoint and 14.2 in (36 cm) is the upper endpoint, so values increase from bottom to top. Its unlabeled interior ticks are harmless subdivisions, the separate BODY LENGTH line repeats the same range, and “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” prevents presentation as the printed bird's physical scale.
The palette swatches correspond to visible and source-supported blue-gray, charcoal, green, purple, and pink-red coloration.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears in the candidate plate.
